Author Vahid Karaahmetovic

Published Nov 23, 2026, 04:51 AM

Investing.com -- U.S. chip and neocloud stocks surged in premarket trading Monday, rebounding from a rout that gave the Nasdaq its worst week since 2020.

Micron, Lam Research and Marvell each rose more than 7% as of 4:43 a.m. ET. SK Hynix’s ADRs gained nearly 10%. Advanced Micro Devices, Intel and Applied Materials climbed more than 6%, and Broadcom added 5.8%. SanDisk rose 7.8% and Seagate 6.8%. 

Nvidia, which has been under pressure recently amid leadership turmoil, gained about 7%. Newly listed Anthropic rose 4.5%. 

Neocloud providers CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN jumped between 8% and 10.5%. 

Broader markets also advanced. Nasdaq 100 futures were up 3.4% and S&P 500 futures 2.6%. Europe’s Stoxx 600 gained 0.7%, led by semiconductor and other technology shares.

Earlier on Monday, authorities in Asia moved to support markets after last week’s wipeout in AI-linked stocks triggered a global selloff in riskier assets. Investors are questioning whether the vast sums going into AI data centers will generate enough profit to justify the spending. Valuations of some AI companies and business models also remain a concern.

Worries about tighter Federal Reserve policy, leadership turmoil at Nvidia and a possible slowdown in AI spending after the U.S. midterms have added to the pressure. 

Nvidia’s premarket gain follows a slide of more than 40% in the shares over the past month. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of the company after acknowledging an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence is reportedly said to believe is a Chinese spy.
